connect.addrHint: We will check that the server answers and learn how many shares it needs.
connect.finishHint: Nothing else to fill in: press Connect and vault management opens. An AppRole can wait — until then the broker uses the root token.
connect.noteHint: The vault note whose fields hold the unseal shares.
connect.rootDone: Root token received and stored in a separate hidden item
connect.rootHint: The shares go to Vault, the token comes back encrypted and lands in a separate hidden item — not next to the shares. It is never shown on screen.
connect.rootWarn: Root is the strongest access there is. Revoke it as soon as an AppRole exists.
connect.sharesHint: Pick the fields holding the shares. The same field twice will not reach the threshold.
danger.title: Danger zone
edit.rootAbsent: No root token. It is issued once, on the first connect.
edit.rootPresent: A root token already exists in the separate hidden item. Issuing a second one gains nothing — the old one keeps working.
edit.sharesKept: Leave empty to keep the shares already chosen.
engine.badPath: Path: letters, digits, dash, underscore, dot, slash, no “..”.
engine.casHint: Force everyone to write with a version. Secrets without their own setting inherit this.
engine.disableAuthConfirm: Every token issued through this method is revoked immediately. Its roles and settings are gone.
engine.disableConfirm: The engine disappears with everything inside: secrets, keys, certificates. There is no way to get them back. Tokens with policies on this path simply stop reaching it.
engine.kind.approle: Login for services and agents: role_id plus secret_id, no human involved. keyward itself uses this.
engine.kind.aws: Temporary AWS access keys from IAM policies instead of permanent ones.
engine.kind.cert: Login with a client TLS certificate.
engine.kind.cubbyhole: Each token's private stash, gone with the token. Built into Vault.
engine.kind.database: Dynamic credentials in PostgreSQL, MySQL and others: each service gets its own short-lived login.
engine.kind.generic: Legacy key → value store, same as kv v1.
engine.kind.github: Login with a GitHub personal token, rights by organisation team.
engine.kind.identity: Vault entities and groups. Built in.
engine.kind.jwt: Login with a JWT from an external issuer: GitLab and GitHub CI pipelines get tokens this way without secrets in settings.
engine.kind.kubernetes: Pod login by cluster service account: a role binds namespace and account to policies.
engine.kind.kv: Key → value store for passwords, tokens, configs. What people usually mean by secrets.
engine.kind.ldap: Login via LDAP or Active Directory, rights by group.
engine.kind.oidc: Login through an SSO provider: Google, Keycloak, Okta. For people, via the browser.
engine.kind.pki: Your own certificate authority: TLS certificates by role, short lifetimes, automatic rotation.
engine.kind.rabbitmq: Dynamic RabbitMQ users with the right vhost permissions.
engine.kind.ssh: SSH certificates and one-time passwords for server access instead of distributing keys.
engine.kind.token: Built-in: Vault tokens themselves. Cannot be disabled.
engine.kind.totp: Generate and verify one-time codes, like an authenticator app.
engine.kind.transit: Encryption as a service: apps send data, Vault encrypts and decrypts with its own key and never hands the key out.
engine.kind.userpass: Username and password stored in Vault itself. For people without SSO.
engine.kvConfig: Version settings for the whole engine
engine.kvV1Hint: Flat store without history: writes overwrite, deletes are permanent. Policy paths are direct.
engine.kvV2Hint: Versions, soft delete, metadata, CAS. Policy paths go through data/ and metadata/. Pick this unless you have a reason not to.
engine.maxTtlHint: Ceiling for renewals. Dynamic secrets (database, aws, pki) do not outlive it.
engine.maxVersionsHint: Versions kept per secret unless the secret sets its own. Empty means 10.
engine.noneAuthHint: Enable approle for services, kubernetes for pods or oidc for people.
engine.noneHint: Enable the first one: kv for secrets, transit for encryption, pki for certificates.
engine.pathHint: All engine paths live under this prefix: secret/… or kv/prod/…. Letters, digits, dashes, slashes.
engine.pathHintAuth: The method is reachable as auth/<path>/login. Usually matches the type.
engine.ttlHint: How long secrets and tokens issued by the engine live unless told otherwise: 1h, 24h, 768h. Empty means the system value.
engine.upgradeConfirm: Irreversible. Policies with direct secret/… paths stop working until rewritten as secret/data/…. Continue?
engine.upgradeHint: Data is kept and becomes version 1 of each secret. There is no way back, and policy paths must be rewritten through data/ and metadata/. The engine is unavailable during migration.
err.chooseNoteForConnection: Choose a note to write the connection into
err.connectionItemMissing: The connection's item was not found — sync the vault
err.durationFormat: {field}: a duration is written as 30m, 24h or 768h
err.engineAbsent: There is no engine {mount} on the server
err.engineNotKv: {path} is an engine of kind {kind}, not kv
err.enginePathCharset: An engine path may hold latin letters, digits, a hyphen, an underscore, a dot and a slash
err.fieldNeedsName: Every field has to have a name
err.kv1DestroyIsTheSecret: KV v1 has no versions: the secret itself is destroyed
err.kv1NoVersions: KV v1 has no version settings
err.kv1NothingToUndelete: KV v1 has no versions, so there is nothing to bring back
err.kvOnlyToV2: KV can be moved only to version 2
err.metadataFieldNeedsName: Every metadata field has to have a name
err.mountIsPartOfVault: {path} is part of Vault itself and cannot be unmounted
err.noAccessorFromServer: The server returned no accessor, so there is nothing to revoke that token with
err.noHiddenRootItem: There is no hidden item with a root token for {addr}
err.noItemWithVaultAddr: The vault has no item with a Vault address
err.noOtpFromServer: The server returned no one-time key, so a root token cannot be generated
err.noRootTokenFor: There is no root token for {addr} in the vault
err.noUnsealFieldsChosen: No fields with shares of the key were chosen
err.noUnsealKeys: The vault item has no unseal keys — fill in kw-vault-unseal
err.noVaultConnectionForItem: This item has no connection to Vault
err.noVaultCredentials: There is nothing to reach Vault with: fill in kw-vault-role-id and kw-vault-secret-id, or kw-vault-token
err.notEnoughShares: Not enough shares: {taken} taken out of {needed}
err.notEnoughUnsealKeys: Not enough keys: {entered} entered out of the {needed} needed
err.otpShorterThanToken: The one-time key is shorter than the token, so there is nothing to decrypt with
err.policyBodyEmpty: An empty policy grants no rights — describe at least one path
err.policyBuiltin: The built-in policy {name} cannot be deleted
err.policyIsRoot: The policy {policy} grants full rights: confirm that separately
err.policyNameCharset: A policy name may hold latin letters, digits, a hyphen, an underscore and a dot
err.policyNameEmpty: An empty policy name means nothing
err.policyNameSlashes: A policy name may hold no slashes and no runs of dots
err.policyNameTooLong: The policy name is longer than 128 characters
err.policyNeedsName: A policy has to have a name
err.policyRequired: At least one policy is needed: without one the token inherits the broker's rights
err.rootNotSavedSoRevoked: The root token was not saved into the vault and so was revoked at once
err.rootRightsHour: Full rights are issued for no longer than an hour
err.rootStranded: The root token was neither saved into the vault nor revoked: a live root token is left on the server, revoke it by hand
err.secretEmpty: There is no point writing an empty secret
err.secretNeedsPath: A secret has to have a path
err.secretPathParent: A secret's path may hold no «..»
err.secretPathTooLong: The secret's path is longer than 512 characters
err.someUnsealFieldsEmpty: Some of the chosen fields are empty, so there is nowhere to take the shares from
err.tokenAuthUndisableable: The token auth method cannot be disabled: Vault itself rests on it
err.ttlOverADay: Longer than a day is no longer temporary access
err.vaultAddrHttps: A Vault address has to start with https://
err.vaultAddrScheme: A Vault address has to start with http:// or https://
err.vaultLockedUnlockIt: The vault is locked; unlock it
err.versionTtlFormat: A version lifetime is written as 30m, 24h or 768h
hashicorp.absentBody: Two ways to connect: reuse an existing vault item that holds the address and keys, or create a new one right here.
hashicorp.approleHint: The broker issues temporary tokens under this role. Rights to auth/token/create and revoke-accessor are enough: a stolen machine still cannot open the vault. Without an AppRole the broker falls back to the root token in the hidden item.
hashicorp.forgetWarn: The address, the AppRole and the pointer to the key shares leave the item. The shares themselves and the root token stay: they are your keys, not ours. If the root is no longer needed, revoke it before disconnecting — afterwards keyward cannot reach it.
hashicorp.namespaceHint: Vault Enterprise only. Leave empty for the open-source server and for OpenBao.
hashicorp.noFields: The chosen note has no fields — there is nowhere to take the keys from
hashicorp.pickVault: Pick a vault on the left
hashicorp.pickVaultHint: Tokens are issued into a specific vault, so that comes first.
hashicorp.sealAuto: The server unseals itself — no keys needed
lint.denyMixed: Deny overrides everything else in this list
lint.duplicatePath: Path “{p}” is already defined above: Vault takes the last block
lint.expectedAttr: An attribute is expected inside the block, not “{t}”
lint.expectedBrace: An opening { is needed after the path
lint.expectedPath: A path block is expected here, not “{t}”
lint.kv2Prefix: {m} is kv v2: the path must go through data/ or metadata/, otherwise the policy grants nothing
lint.listNeedsStrings: Lists take quoted strings only, not “{t}”
lint.noCapabilities: Block “{p}” has no capabilities — it neither allows nor denies anything
lint.sudo: Sudo on “{p}” — access to protected system paths, nearly root
lint.unknownAttr: Vault does not know the attribute “{a}”
lint.unknownCapability: No such capability: “{c}”. Valid: create, read, update, patch, delete, list, sudo, deny
lint.unknownMount: No engine “{m}” is visible on the server — the path may be wrong
plugin.hashicorp.description: A broker for temporary access to HashiCorp Vault
plugin.hashicorp.title: Vault
policy.adminHint: A short-lived token that can create and edit Vault policies — to bootstrap a service without root. Counts as full privileges: separate consent, one hour at most. The policy itself lives only while a token carrying it is alive; then the daemon deletes it from Vault.
policy.deleteConfirm: Tokens carrying this policy lose its rights immediately; issued accesses stay listed in the registry. The only way back is to create the policy again.
policy.empty: This policy has no body: it is built into Vault.
policy.hist.restoreHint: Bring back this state. The restore itself lands in history and can be undone with ⌘Z.
policy.name: Name
policy.nameHint: Latin letters, digits, dashes. The token refers to the policy by this name.
policy.studio.formatHint: Canonical form: indentation, capability order, blank lines between blocks
policy.studio.help1: Ctrl+Space or just type: inside the quotes after path you get engine and system paths, inside capabilities you get the rights.
policy.studio.help2: “Insert block” adds a ready block at the cursor without overwriting anything. kv v2 paths go through data/ and metadata/.
policy.studio.help3: Underlines are live checks: red will not save, yellow deserves a look, blue is just a note.
policy.unknownWhat: Cannot read the paths — open it under Policies
policy.what: A policy is a list of Vault paths and rights on them. The token gets exactly what it says and nothing more. Not sure which one — press New: the path comes from the list of engines, the rights from three options.
root.dead: The server does not know it
root.noneHint: No root was issued for {addr} — or it is already revoked.
root.revokeBody: The token for {addr} stops working immediately. If the broker runs on it and no AppRole exists, issuing stops too.
root.warn: Root opens the whole vault. There is no reason to keep it longer than setting up an AppRole takes.
secret.badPath: “..” is not allowed in the path.
secret.casConflict: The secret changed while you were editing. Close, reopen and redo the edit on the fresh version.
secret.casRequiredHint: Writes must name the version they edited. Protects against blind overwrites.
secret.customMetadataHint: Non-secret notes: owner, ticket, purpose. Readable with the metadata, without access to values.
secret.deleteAfterHint: A duration like 720h or 30m; empty means forever.
secret.deleteConfirmV1: KV v1: the secret disappears for good, it has no history.
secret.deleteConfirmV2: The latest version is marked deleted: data is hidden but recoverable from the version list. Older versions are untouched.
secret.deleteZoneV1: Delete the secret for good: kv v1 has no history.
secret.deleteZoneV2: Hide the latest version. Data stays and can be restored from the version list.
secret.destroyConfirm: This version's data is gone for good. The version stays in history marked as destroyed.
secret.emptyHint: No folders or secrets at this path. Press “New secret” to write the first one.
secret.engineV1: KV v1: no versions, deletion is permanent
secret.engineV2: KV v2: versions, soft delete, metadata
secret.envHint: KEY=VALUE lines. “export” and quotes are stripped; \n and \" work inside double quotes.
secret.jsonHint: A “key → string” object, like in the Vault UI. Numbers and nested objects are stored as strings.
secret.maxVersionsHint: 0 uses the engine setting (usually 10). Older ones are pruned automatically.
secret.needFields: At least one named field is needed.
secret.noMountsHint: Secrets live in kv engines. Enable one in Vault and it shows up here.
secret.pathHint: Slashes make folders. A path ending without a name won't do.
secret.purgeConfirm: Every version and the metadata are wiped with no way back.
secret.purgeZone: Wipe every version and the metadata with no way back.
secret.rollbackConfirm: Version {v} data is written as a new version on top of the current one ({cur}). Nothing is deleted; history stays intact.
secret.viewingOld: Showing version {v}, not the current one.
secret.writeHintV1: KV v1: writing replaces the secret entirely, no history.
secret.writeHintV2: Written whole as a new version; the previous one stays in Vault's history.
settings.expiryNoticesHint: A system notification when issued access is about to expire and when it has.
vault.defaultPolicy: Vault always adds default to the chosen policies: it lets the token look itself up, renew and revoke itself. Without it Vault clients declare the token invalid — they start with a lookup-self check.
vault.issuedOnce: Shown once — after this you can only revoke it.
vault.needPolicy: Pick at least one policy — without it the token gets no rights
vault.noIssuesHint: Issued access will appear here with time left and a revoke button.
vault.sealedBody: {p} of {t} keys entered. It can be unsealed with the stored ones — they live in the vault item.
vault.unwrapHow: This is an envelope, not a token. The recipient runs once: vault unwrap <code> — and gets the token.
vault.usesHint: Vault gets {n}: one use goes to the client's own self-check (vault login, lookup-self).
vault.usesN: {n}, one of them goes to the client's self-check
vault.wideHint: The {p} policy equals root: it can do anything, including minting new roots. Such a token lives an hour at most.
vault.wrapHint: The recipient gets a one-time code instead of the token and swaps it for the token with vault unwrap. If the swap was already done, someone intercepted it. Never put this code into VAULT_TOKEN.
